about:
Badlands Steel operates from Williston, North Dakota, where it was established to meet a growing regional demand for steel fabrication. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its origins trace back to a recognized need for comprehensive fabrication services in the Williston area.

The shop fabricates products from carbon steel, aluminum, and stainless steel, offering a range of steel products and services. It describes its equipment as state-of-the-art and capable of handling all aspects of steel fabrication, though specific machinery, facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not publicly detailed.

Badlands Steel serves customers in the oil field, natural gas, industrial, construction, and agriculture sectors. These five industries are explicitly listed on the company’s website as its primary markets.

The company emphasizes a devotion to high-quality products and the use of modern equipment to cover the full scope of fabrication needs, positioning itself as a single-source provider for hard-to-find metal products.

name: Baker Medical, Inc.
old_description: is a locally-owned and operated medical supply store based in Conway, Arkansas. For more than 10 years, we've been helping individuals and healthcare professionals from all over the state of Arkansas care for themselves and their patients by offering medical supplies and equipment.
about:
Baker Medical, Inc. is a locally owned medical supply company headquartered in Conway, Arkansas, with a second location in Clinton. The business has served the state for nearly two decades, operating as an independent retailer of medical equipment and supplies.

The company distributes a range of home healthcare products, including CPAP and BiPAP systems, catheters, incontinence supplies, diabetic and insulin pump accessories, and oral nutritional supplements. A respiratory therapist on staff performs CPAP setups and manages a resupply program that ships replacement items directly to patients. Orders are processed within one business day and shipped free via USPS for purchases over $20, reaching any Arkansas address in two to three business days.

Baker Medical serves both individual patients and healthcare professionals throughout Arkansas. Its customer base includes sleep therapy patients, urology and incontinence care recipients, and individuals managing diabetes. The company bills most insurance plans with a valid prescription, acting as a liaison between patients and payers.

The firm emphasizes personalized service, citing its respiratory therapist’s daily involvement and a commitment to rapid order fulfillment as key differentiators. Its slogan, “A BETTER NIGHT’S SLEEP IS ONLY A PHONE CALL AWAY,” reflects a focus on sleep therapy as a core specialty.

name: Balance Clothing Company
old_description: is becoming more and more popular, and it just so happens to be one of our specialties! We have developed quite the reputation as the go-to vinyl shop around town, and are constantly expanding our client base. We currently have clients in Chicago, Columbus, Cincinnati, and even Hawaii!
about:
Balance Clothing Company operates from Charleston, West Virginia, where it was founded in 2007 by David Collins. Collins started the business while searching for harmony among the creative process, printing, and design, and the company has grown steadily since its inception.

The firm functions as a custom art agency with an in-house screen printing and vinyl workshop. Its production capabilities span screen printing on apparel, vinyl wrapping for vehicles, boats, buildings, and walls, as well as large-format output such as posters, banners, feather flags, and corrugated plastic signs. The shop also produces rigid signage including 3-D lettering, Lexan and metal signs, trade show booth backdrops, tents, canopies, and a full range of print collateral from business cards to brochures.

Balance serves clients across multiple states, with noted accounts in Chicago, Columbus, Cincinnati, and Hawaii. Its customer base includes businesses seeking branded apparel, vehicle and marine graphics, architectural signage, and trade show displays, as well as individuals looking for custom stickers, banners, and promotional items.

Collins launched the company to unify design and production under one roof, a philosophy that still drives the operation. The team pairs each project with a dedicated artist to tailor files for print, continuously sources new apparel styles and vinyl materials, and emphasizes building long-term relationships over transactional jobs.

name: Bald Ridge Enterprises, LLC
old_description: Bald Ridge Enterprises is the trusted name for sheet metal in Wyoming and Montana, delivering precision craftsmanship in architectural sheet metal and metal construction. From custom roofing and siding to premanufactured metal buildings, our work is built to perform and designed to last.
about:
Bald Ridge Enterprises operates from Cody, Wyoming, serving customers across Wyoming and Montana. The company was founded nearly four decades ago on family values and a dedication to craftsmanship, growing from a small local shop into a recognized contractor. It is certified as a Women-Owned Small Business with US Federal Contractor Registration.

The company provides complete metal construction services with all fabrication performed in-house. Its capabilities include pre-manufactured steel buildings, metal roofing systems, metal siding and exterior components (soffits, fascia, gutters, downspouts), specialty metalwork such as snow bars and chimney caps, and carpentry. The team handles design, fabrication, and installation for projects of varying scale.

Bald Ridge serves commercial, agricultural, residential, institutional, and government clients. Examples include custom roofing and siding for homes, pre-engineered steel buildings for farms and commercial facilities, and architectural sheet metal for institutional and government projects throughout the two-state region.

The company emphasizes in-house fabrication for quality control, adherence to the Architectural Sheet Metal Manual, and engineering for the harsh weather conditions of Wyoming and Montana. Its family-focused culture and status as a women-owned small business are cited as key differentiators, along with standard one-year warranties and extended manufacturer guarantees.

The company serves residential homeowners, local contractors, and architects, with a notable portfolio in marine and architectural metalwork. Customers include individuals seeking custom countertops or fireplace surrounds, as well as commercial clients needing HVAC components and tank fabrication.

Ballard emphasizes its team’s experience and certified welders as differentiators, promoting in-house fabrication and installation to maintain tight tolerances and reduce seams.

about:
Barbett Industries Inc. operates from Reading, Pennsylvania, where it has built a business around narrow-fabric manufacturing. The company is led by President Frank J. Loos and General Manager Joseph Loos, his son, indicating a family-led operation. No founding year is disclosed in public materials.

The firm produces a broad line of narrow textiles including twist cord, draw cord, lamp shade trim, Chinese braid, bolo cord, industrial braid, metallic braid, jacquard braids, shoelaces, boot laces, bullion fringe, soutache, and vellum braid. Finishing capabilities cover custom dyeing, acetate tipping, hot and cold cutting, metal barbing, cord and tassel assembly, textile crimping, and waxing. The company also replicates customer samples and provides production cost estimates, and it accepts customer-supplied goods for finishing work.

Barbett serves the apparel, military and uniform, home furnishings, industrial, fishing lure, and flag component markets. Its product categories also include braided vinyl and leather trims. Customers range from original equipment manufacturers to uniform suppliers and specialty fabricators.

The company positions itself as an independent domestic source for both custom and commodity narrow fabrics, emphasizing competitive pricing and the ability to match customer samples. It highlights its willingness to process customer-owned materials through its finishing operations.

name: Barku Plastics
old_description: Barku has been producing high-quality plastic parts for 40 years. Precision parts using injection molding technology as well as profiles and pipes using extrusion processes are manufactured quickly and reliably.
about:
Barku Plastics operates from Cleveland, Tennessee. The U.S. subsidiary was established in September 2003 by its German parent, Barku Kunststofftechnik GmbH, which traces its origins to 1 October 1977 when Egon Schumacher founded it as a subsidiary of LUBING Maschinenfabrik GmbH. The American operation began as an extension of that German expertise into the North American market.

The company produces precision plastic components through injection molding and profile extrusion. Its Cleveland plant runs more than 50 injection molding machines ranging from 32 to 1,100 tons, capable of two-component and insert molding, alongside over 10 extrusion lines that handle diameters up to 6 inches and profile widths up to 39 3/8 inches, including co-extrusion for multi-material profiles. Annual raw material throughput exceeds 14,000 tons, and the facility operates on a three-shift schedule.

Barku serves customers worldwide, working with mold builders on three continents and providing value-added assembly, engineering support, and custom mold development. Its parts and profiles find use in applications requiring tight tolerances and consistent quality, though the company does not publicly list specific end-market sectors.

The firm emphasizes flexibility, continuous investment in machinery, and ongoing employee training to optimize processes and meet delivery schedules. Its quality management system is certified to ISO 9001:2015 by TÜV Rheinland, reflecting a stated commitment to continuous improvement and stringent quality standards.

name: Barn XO
old_description: It’s our privilege to reclaim rare Midwestern woods originally harvested during Chicago’s industrial rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s. Their rich history lives on through every knot, grain, and imperfection.
about:
Barn XO is a family-owned furniture maker based in Mundelein, Illinois, that specializes in custom pieces crafted from reclaimed Midwestern woods. The company sources timber originally harvested during Chicago's industrial rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s, preserving the material's history in each knot and grain pattern.

The workshop produces a range of handcrafted items including conference tables, dining and bar tables, chairs, bar stools, desks, console tables, and coffee tables. Each piece is built to order through a process that begins with a design consultation, either online or at the company's Mundelein showroom, followed by material selection and fabrication. Finished goods are shipped nationwide from the Illinois facility.

Barn XO serves both residential and commercial clients. Homeowners commission dining tables, benches, and live-edge desks, while businesses order custom conference tables and collaborative work surfaces. Customer reviews reference direct communication with the owners and project updates throughout the build process.

The company positions its work at the intersection of sustainability and timeless craftsmanship, emphasizing that its furniture carries the history of its origins. By reclaiming wood that would otherwise be discarded, Barn XO aims to create unique, durable pieces that reduce demand for newly harvested lumber.

name: Barrett Petfood
old_description: Barrett Petfood was founded on a simple promise: If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products. We help pets and pet food companies thrive by delivering a premium manufacturing and brand services experience that takes pet food from idea to bowl with integrity.
about:
Barrett Petfood operates from Brainerd, Minnesota, where it was founded in 2006. The company began when agricultural entrepreneur Mike Barrett purchased a piece of equipment intended for agricultural manufacturing, only to realize it was designed for food production. Seeing an opportunity, Mike and his children, Tom and Sarah Barrett, pivoted into the pet food industry. Mike later transitioned ownership to Tom and Sarah, while he continued supplying ingredients from his farm.

Today, Barrett runs two facilities: the original Brainerd plant and a 160,000-square-foot facility in Little Falls, Minnesota, opened in 2020 with two additional production lines. The company offers extrusion, freeze-drying, milling, and automated packaging, producing hundreds of formulas for dogs, cats, reptiles, birds, livestock, and zoo animals. Its services span diet formulation, ingredient sourcing, processing, packaging, and global distribution.

Barrett serves emerging and established pet food brands seeking a co-manufacturing partner. Its customer base includes companies in the super-premium kibble and kibble-plus categories, as well as brands requiring specialized diets for exotic and farm animals. The company positions itself as an extension of its partners' teams, handling supply chain logistics and production details.

The business was built on a simple promise: “If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products.” Tom and Sarah Barrett emphasize a relationship-based philosophy, personal involvement in each brand, and a “Don’t Say No” mindset that drives innovation. They cite transparency, integrity, and rigorous food-safety standards as key differentiators.
